title: Blink
description: Turn an external LED on and off, once a second, using digitalWrite().

steps.clip: Grab an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, one LED, one 1 kΩ resistor and a few jumper wires.
Push the resistor into the breadboard, with its two legs in two different numbered columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round — it doesn't matter which leg goes where.
Each numbered column is one connection, so the two legs need two different columns.
steps.goal: Put the resistor on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Take a jumper wire. Push one end into a free hole in the same column as one of the resistor's legs, and the other end into pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin 13 is on the Arduino's top row of sockets, next to GND.
Any free hole in that column works — the five holes of a column (a–e) are joined.
steps.goal: Connect one end of the resistor to pin 13.

steps.clip: Now the LED. Its legs are different lengths: put the long leg in the same column as the resistor's other leg, and the short leg in an empty column next to it. Sharing a column already connects them — no wire needed.
hints: The long leg is the + side (the anode). The LED only lights if it points toward the resistor.
Two legs in the same column are already connected — you don't need a wire.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the free end of the resistor.

steps.clip: Take another jumper wire. Put one end in a free hole in the LED's short-leg column, and the other end into a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: The short leg is the − side (the cathode). It goes to ground.
Any GND pin on the Arduino works — they're all connected inside the board.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. The LED should blink: on for one second, off for one second.
